newsitem.title: USA: NYPA trims 780 MW power plant output for repairs.
newsitem.headline: NYPA trims 780 MW power plant output for repairs.

text.p: New York Power Authority's (NYPA) Fitzpatrick nuclear power plant was producing electricity at reduced capacity while repairing a reactor feed pump, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
The 780 megawatt (MW) station in Scriba, N.Y., was operating at 60 percent of capacity, according to the NRC's Wednesday daily status report.
The Fitzpatrick plant tripped off line Sept 16 when a technician caused an electrical short, which in turn opened the generator output breakers and automatically shut the reactor.
NYPA earlier said it hoped to return the nuclear station to full output some time today.
NYPA officials were not immediately available for comment about the feed pump repair.
Indian Point 3, NYPA's other nuclear plant, was producing electricity at its full 980 MW capacity, the NRC reported.
NYPA provides about a fourth of New York's electricity.
